clue.text: Working with home decor, salesman doing a dance, having offloaded first item

indicators.note: to offload the first item is to drop the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
doing a dance is capering; its opening C goes

explanation.surface: A salesman jigs about clumsily while handling a load of soft furnishings.
explanation.walkthrough: Capering is skipping about merrily; losing its C leaves the tail that follows REP.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting fresh wallpaper on rooms is a decorating job, so someone doing it is working on interior finish.

clue.text: Fellow amongst celebrities is a potential winner

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
a plain synonym: amongst means in
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone mixing with the famous looks set to take a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amongst' looks like an instruction to put one piece inside another, but here it simply supplies its own synonym, read straight through; the A-list is the top tier of fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who reaches the last round still has a chance of taking the title.

clue.text: Announcement from mobile seller offering cool stuff?

definitions.text: Announcement from mobile seller offering cool stuff?

blocks.note: surface reading: a trader with a phone, or a vendor of mobile phones
setter's reading: a travelling ice-cream vendor whose wares are literally cold

explanation.walkthrough: This was the slogan painted on Wall's ice-cream tricycles in Britain from the 1920s; the cyclist sold ice cream on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a famous British street-vendor slogan inviting passers-by to flag down the bike and purchase a frozen treat.

clue.text: Is a big story upsetting tennis star?

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting turns things upside down, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a saga is a long epic tale

explanation.surface: A question whether some scandal is causing distress to a sporting celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' pretends to describe the effect of the story on the star; it actually flips the letters of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is an American former world number one who won eight Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: What's going down around rear of car, alerting after a crash?

definitions.text: What's going down around rear of car, alerting after a crash?

indicators.note: the rear of something is its tail end, so only the final letter is kept
to go around something is to enclose it on both sides
a crash leaves things jumbled, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: something waning is going down, like the moon
the final letter of car
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of what gets placed on the road behind a vehicle to alert other drivers after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the device is literally set down behind the rear of the car to alert after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists place this red reflective sign on the road behind a broken-down or crashed vehicle to caution approaching traffic.

clue.text: Hide whip - side of door satisfactory?

blocks.note: a jamb is the upright side post of a door frame
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to conceal a whip beside the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb telling you to conceal something, but it is the leather the whip is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A jambok, or sjambok, is a heavy South African whip traditionally cut from rhinoceros or hippo leather.

clue.text: British currency - one old penny with Queen on

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: Qu. is an abbreviation for queen
the Roman numeral for one
d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: An old British penny bearing the monarch's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money was pounds, shillings and pence, written £sd, with d for the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is the everyday British slang term for one pound sterling.

clue.text: Ex-serviceman embracing daughter is a learned Hindu

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms round, so one piece surrounds the rest

blocks.note: vet is short for veteran
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former soldier hugging his daughter turns out to be a scholar of Hindu scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link before the definition, but it belongs inside the wordplay; the definition is just 'a learned Hindu'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vedist is someone deeply versed in the Vedas, the oldest sacred scriptures of Hinduism.

clue.text: Tropical tree: a copper is behind one in American Pacific island

indicators.note: being behind something means following it, so this piece comes second
being in something means sitting inside it, enclosed on both sides

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: A botanical note mixed up with a police officer stationed on a US island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, by its chemical symbol. The island splits before its final letter to take the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Guaiacum is a genus of small Caribbean and tropical American trees, the source of lignum vitae hardwood.

clue.text: Lions and tigers etc circling mountain area for flowering plants

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: lions and tigers are big cats
an alp is a high mountain
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Big cats prowl round a mountain region in search of blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Etc' signals a general category for the examples, here the cat family as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalpas are deciduous trees with large heart-shaped leaves and showy clusters of white blossoms, so they count as flowering plants.

clue.text: Unnoticed person turned on by lad bearing diamonds

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards
by means next to, so one piece is placed alongside another
to bear is to carry, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
a lad is a boy
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An overlooked figure becomes attractive to a young man wearing jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' reads as aroused, but 'on' is the letters to flip. 'Person' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a nobody means they are insignificant and go unregarded by others.

clue.text: Man, hero, chasing Persian spirit in hottest place

indicators.note: what chases comes after its quarry, so these pieces follow the other

blocks.note: a peri is a fairy-like being in Persian mythology
he is a man, as a pronoun
a lion is a celebrated, brave person

explanation.surface: A heroic man pursues a spirit into somewhere scorching, perhaps hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hottest place' suggests hell or a desert, but it is astronomy: the point in an orbit that is warmest.
explanation.definitionFit: The perihelion is the point of a planet's orbit closest to the Sun, where it receives the most solar heat.

clue.text: Keen on her lipstick, primarily, and eye makeup

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A woman fond of her lipstick also likes something for her eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like the start of the definition, but every word up to 'primarily' is just the source of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohl is a black powder used to darken the rims of the eyelids, a cosmetic of ancient origin.

clue.text: Passionate lot excited about Bishop coming in wearing a cowl

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and stirred up, so the letters get jumbled
about means round and about, so the extra letter is mixed in with the rest
coming in means entering, so this group goes inside another
something worn covers whoever wears it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
someone in a cowl is hooded

explanation.surface: An agitated crowd surrounds a bishop who arrives dressed in a monk's hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot excited about Bishop' is one unit: the bishop's letter joins the jumble. A cowl is a monk's hood, so wearing one makes you hooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-blooded people are ardent and quick to anger, so the adjective matches someone full of strong emotion.

clue.text: Mean clue, missing start and finish

indicators.note: missing its start means lacking the opening letter, which is dropped

blocks.note: a clue is a hint, minus its H
the finish is the end

explanation.surface: A complaint about a nasty clue that has lost both its first and last letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing start and finish' looks like one instruction to trim both ends; in fact only the start is missing, and 'finish' supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to plan or have it as a purpose, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A couple of times sumo wrestling, at the maximum

definitions.note: the answer is the noun in 'at the utmost'; the clue gives the whole phrase

indicators.note: wrestlers grapple and twist each other about, so the letters are thrown into new order

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time, taken twice
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Two bouts of sumo wrestling, each pushed as far as it will go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sumo wrestling' reads as the sport, but 'wrestling' is the instruction acting on SUMO and the two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to the utmost means doing it to the greatest possible degree, the highest extent available.

clue.text: Work on network involves writer describing many an office

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first
to involve is to include within, so one piece takes in another

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
a pen is a writing instrument
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A writer's job includes working on a computer network in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the work above the network; the writer then goes in after the first letter. Op is short for opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office has no internal walls, a layout common in modern workplaces, so the term characterises them.

clue.text: Dead period recalled, by Jove!

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on remembering a long-gone era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests memory, but it means bring back, reversing D plus AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of surprise; egad is a mild oath from 'ah God'.

clue.text: Fierce character in newspaper probing academic

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a don is a university lecturer
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A ferocious figure from a newspaper investigates a university scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow or tutor at Oxford or Cambridge; a rag is a low-quality newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a formidable, intimidating person, often used of a stern woman, so a fierce character.

clue.text: Artist, extravagant in book pair presented about small group

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, between its parts
about means around, so the outer piece wraps round what follows

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
OTT is short for over the top
two as a Roman numeral
a cell is a small unit within an organisation

explanation.surface: A showy painter is featured in a book, two of them about a little group.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers at once: the Roman two splits around the group, then 'extravagant' (the abbreviation for over the top) slips in after the book's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandro Botticelli was an Italian Renaissance painter, famous for The Birth of Venus.

clue.text: Demanding hint about soccer team

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a tang is a trace or hint of flavour
a football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A pushy suggestion regarding a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demanding' looks like it describes the hint, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taxing is hard work and makes heavy demands on one's energy or patience.

clue.text: Surprised comment about unknown guy having female's address

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes either side of the rest

blocks.note: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise
Y is an algebraic unknown
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: An exclamation at finding a mystery man living at a woman's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a street location, but it means a form of words used to speak to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: My lady is a respectful way to speak to a woman of noble rank, a form of address.

clue.text: Frenchman certainly welcoming reduced volume

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in a guest, so one piece receives another

blocks.note: yes, certainly
volume shortened to its abbreviation V

explanation.surface: A Frenchman happily accepts turning the sound down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' tells you to abbreviate volume, not that something is quieter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yves is a common French given name, as in the designer Yves Saint Laurent.

clue.text: Element subsuming phosphorus, hydrogen and oxygen suggests Greek writer

indicators.note: to subsume is to take into a larger whole, so one piece absorbs the rest

blocks.note: xenon is a noble gas element
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry formula of several elements somehow points to an ancient author.
explanation.walkthrough: All the pieces are chemical symbols, and the three single letters go inside XENON before its last N.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophon was an Athenian historian and soldier, author of the Anabasis, so an ancient Hellenic author.

clue.text: Target Buddhism? Foreign King never engaged in that

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be inside it, occupied within

blocks.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism
roi is French for king
no, as in not at all

explanation.surface: Questioning whether Buddhism is a target, since a foreign monarch never practised it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' points back to Buddhism, which takes in the other two pieces. The foreign king is French: roi.
explanation.definitionFit: To zero in on something is to aim at it precisely, so the verb phrase matches the verb target.

clue.text: Dull start, and little energy before conclusion of competition

indicators.note: before means ahead of, so this piece is placed first
a conclusion is the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: to have the lead is to be in front from the start
E is the symbol for energy, reduced to a single letter
the final letter of competition

explanation.surface: A race that begins sluggishly, with the runners flagging just before the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull start' reads as one phrase about a slow beginning, but 'Dull' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy and lifeless, like lead itself, so it describes something tedious or grey.
